title: Composite evaluation harness for mixed-metric quality scoring across FP8/INT8 quantized profiles
creator: Asha Nair
description:
Build a reusable evaluation harness that computes a composite quality score for quantized model profiles (FP8 and INT8). The harness will standardize metric collection across perplexity, MMLU-style multi-choice suites, ROUGE/BLEU for generation tasks, and a plugin interface for task-specific scorers (e.g., semantic similarity, info-extraction F1). Outputs must be exportable to the Console's metrics backend and support differential comparisons vs a pinned fp32 baseline and between quant profiles.

Goals:
- Provide a single invocation that runs dataset partitions (eval/train slices) and emits per-task metrics plus a weighted composite score.
- Support configurable weight maps per project and per-task thresholds for gating (accept / flag / fail).
- Integrate into the existing calibration workflow: after calibration artifacts are produced, run the harness automatically as a post-calibration validation step.
- Emit structured artifacts (JSONL per-run) suitable for dashboards, regression alerts, and archiving to S3.

Non-goals:
- Model-internal calibration algorithm changes (this ticket assumes calibration produces quant profiles already).
- Replacing specialized offline eval frameworks; we will integrate them via adapters.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness runs end-to-end against an FP32 baseline and two quant profiles (fp8, int8) and generates a per-task metrics JSON and a single composite score JSON.
2) Support for perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, ROUGE-L and BLEU-4, and a plugin scorer API for custom tasks documented in the repo README.
3) Composite score uses a configurable weight map and exposes both weighted and unweighted results.
4) Regression gating runs in CI: if composite drop > configured delta or any per-task drop exceeds threshold, the run fails and posts a Slack alert to #quant-evals.
5) Artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/{run_id}/ and Console dashboard shows the new run within 15 minutes.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: lightweight runner written in Python, built on top of the existing eval harness adapters (see ENG-6241). Core components:
- dataset loader shim (supports S3 and local fixtures)
- metric orchestration layer that maps tasks to metric functions
- plugin interface (python entrypoint) for task-specific scorers (must implement score(preds, refs, config) -> {metric_name: value})
- aggregator that computes per-task, per-suite, and global composite scores via a weight map yaml
- result serializer (JSONL per-example + run_summary.json) and uploader to S3

Design decisions / trade-offs noted during kickoff:
- Use existing MMLU runner for multi-choice to preserve compatibility; wrap outputs into our schema rather than reimplementing scoring. Trade-off: small duplication of parsing logic to normalize outputs.
- Perplexity will be computed using token-level log-prob outputs when available; for models that do not surface logits in the hosted mode, fall back to surrogate perplexity (cross-entropy approximations) and mark in metadata.
- For generation tasks with ROUGE/BLEU, use sacrebleu and rouge_score libs to ensure consistent tokenization.

Integration points:
- Post-calibration pipeline (calibration-orchestrator) will invoke the harness once calibration artifacts are available.
- Console export: upload run_summary.json to metrics ingestion endpoint with run_id and profile_tag labels.
test_plan:
Unit tests for aggregator, plugin API, and serializer.
Integration tests: run harness against small synthetic datasets for fp32, fp8, and int8 profiles in CI with mocked S3 and mocked Console ingestion.
Performance test: ensure end-to-end run for standard MMLU + 3 generation tasks completes within 30 minutes on evaluation infra (ci-eval-large).
Acceptance tests: manual run with internal dataset (s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/manual-sets/quant-smoke/) validating Slack alerting and Console visibility.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge to feature branch and run CI integration tests.
2) Run canary on calibration staging pipeline (10% of calibrations) for two weeks, monitor composite deltas and per-task regressions.
3) If canary stable, flip default to run for all calibrations; provide opt-out flag for large customers.
4) Post-rollout: collect two weeks of runs and create a dashboard comparing fp32->fp8 and fp32->int8 deltas per-team.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: aligned with PM on weight map defaults and gating philosophy. PM recommends conservative default weights (MMLU:0.4, perplexity:0.2, rouge:0.25, bleU:0.15) pending calibration per-task sensitivity study (see follow-up).

2026-02-18 - Design review: Eng + Eval team preferred pluggable scorer API. Ben (Eval lead) suggested including confidence metadata per-example to enable uncertainty-weighted aggregation. We captured this as an extension for v2.

2026-02-25 - Implementation started: scaffolded harness and plugin interface. Created feature branch feat/composite-eval/ENG-158932. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-evals/pull/748

2026-03-03 - Trade-off discussion: Decided to compute perplexity from token log-probs when available; for hosted-only models lacking logits we will estimate using predictive likelihood approximations and annotate results. This avoids blocking adoption for hosted customers but requires clear labeling in Console.

2026-03-07 - QA note: Running baseline smoke tests against sample MMLU and summarization sets. Observed that int8 profile for summarization has ROUGE-L drop of 3.2 points vs fp32. Marked for calibration re-run (ENG-52730).

2026-03-12 - CI: Integration tests passed against mocked S3 and Console ingestion. Uploaded artifacts to s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/feat-ENG-158932/canary-2026-03-12/. Triggered Slack alert to #quant-evals on intentional failure test. Next: enable staging pipeline canary.

2026-03-14 - PR reviewer feedback from Mira (Runtime): requested clearer schema for run_summary.json with explicit metric versioning and model_metadata fields. Added schema draft to Confluence and pushed update to PR.
